It follows the structure described in **Session 38 (2025‑05‑16)** and the related concepts [[concepts/budgeting]], [[concepts/payday‑timing]], [[concepts/buffer]], [[concepts/essential‑expenses]], [[concepts/investment‑automation]]. --- ## 1. Timing (payday‑based automation) Assuming a **bi‑monthly pay schedule** (1st & 15th of each month): | Paydate | Automation steps | |---------|-------------------| | **1st** | 1️⃣ Transfer the **full amount for rent and all fixed bills** to the Bills account.
2️⃣ Transfer **½ of the monthly investment/savings goal** to the chosen savings/investment account.
3️⃣ Keep a **buffer** in the Bills account (see §3). | | **15th** | 1️⃣ Transfer the **remaining ½ of the investment/savings amount**.
2️⃣ Top‑up the Bills account for any later‑month subscriptions or variable bills.
3️⃣ Any leftover goes to the Flexible‑spending account. | > This schedule is the “Practical Example Schedule” from the summary and aligns with the **payday‑timing** concept [[concepts/payday‑timing]]. --- ## 3. How big should the buffer be? | Situation | Suggested buffer | |-----------|------------------| | You **pay rent** (or a similar large fixed housing cost) | **$200 – $300** | | You **don’t have rent** (e.g., living with family, own home mortgage already covered) | **$150 – $200** | The buffer sits in the Bills/checking account and absorbs unpredictable charges (utility spikes, subscription creep). Adjust upward only if you notice frequent shortfalls [[concepts/buffer]]. --- ## 4. Setting the amounts 1. **Calculate net monthly income** (after taxes). 2. **Subtract** all **essential fixed expenses** (rent, utilities, insurance, debt).
